summary: Source-anchored research for custom $accumulator spill and merge semantics. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The $accumulator lifecycle initializes state with init, updates it per document with accumulate, merges intermediate states when needed (including merging results from each shard on a sharded cluster), and applies the optional finalize once all documents have been processed. This is documented by MongoDB. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md

merge receives two intermediate states and returns their combined state; when more states remain, MongoDB repeatedly merges the combined state with another state. This callback is distinct from the $merge output stage. (high confidence)

A compact average implementation retains sum and count, adds corresponding fields when merging partial states, and divides only in finalize. This is a documented pattern for preserving sufficient intermediate state across merges. (high confidence)

In the 2023 MongoDB 6.0.8 forum investigation, Jason Tran could not reproduce the reporter's failure with the supplied workload, including a later run processing roughly 10,000 documents. The thread does not establish a confirmed root cause. (low confidence)

MongoDB documents that spilling to disk or running on a sharded cluster can make an $accumulator be computed as a merge of multiple sub-accumulations, each starting with init(), so init(), accumulate() and merge() must be compatible with this model. The merge function always merges two states at a time, repeatedly, and document processing order can vary. Design inference (not a documented API contract): because of this, making merge order-independent and associative is a sensible target. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md

MongoDB's migration example keeps count and quantity in the intermediate state, adds both fields when merging, and computes their ratio in finalize. This illustrates retaining mergeable sufficient statistics instead of prematurely averaging partial outputs. (medium confidence)

Studio 3T demonstrates a custom accumulator that initializes an empty city array, appends city names in accumulate, concatenates two arrays in merge, and joins the array into a string in finalize. The example demonstrates a growing intermediate state rather than a fixed-size summary. (low confidence)

MongoDB documents that spilling with allowDiskUse can save an in-progress custom accumulator operation to disk and later combine disk and memory states through its merge callback. Each sub-accumulation starts with init(). (low confidence)

A preceding $sort does not guarantee the processing order observed by custom init, accumulate, or merge functions. MongoDB explicitly warns against custom accumulators whose correctness requires a particular document order. (low confidence)

Historical reports describe Out of memory despite allowDiskUse for custom $accumulator workloads on MongoDB 4.4.1 and 6.0.8. These reports show that enabling disk use is not evidence that every workload will complete; they do not identify a universal byte threshold or establish present-version behavior. (medium confidence) Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-51340 ; https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/allowdiskuse-has-no-effect-in-case-of-accumulator/236724

MongoDB documents that disk spilling or sharded execution can split a custom $accumulator into multiple sub-accumulations, each beginning with init(); init, accumulate, and merge must support that execution model. (low confidence)
